endorsements.quote: Instead, it is important to notify subjects of the risks associated with the intended reuse and provide them with the opportunity to refuse or withdraw ( 30 ), when feasible.
Regular security assessments and audits are integral to promptly identifying and addressing vulnerabilities.
Comprehensive measures include advanced encryption, rigorous access controls, and continuous monitoring for breaches.

As federated learning on its own is not a fully privacy-preserving method, it must be combined with formal privacy techniques such as differential privacy or cryptography ( 18 – 20 ) to prevent cyber security attacks from, for example, extracting sensitive data from the AI-based models ( 21 ).

Automated systems in patient care must be regularly monitored to identify any algorithmic discrimination due to unforeseen interactions with unaddressed inequities, postdeployment changes, or shifts in patient data and context.
Although demanding extensive effort and data, specification of limitations for particular populations, imaging equipment, or tasks is essential for trustworthy TDTs.
In the interim, ensuring transparency about the intended uses and accuracy of TDTs might be adequate for clinicians to adequately inform patients about the risks and benefits.
Ownership of TDTs, especially in interconnected systems, requires clear contracts to allocate liability.
The ongoing process of risk management also involves collaboration with regulatory bodies to remain compliant with evolving guidelines.

unlisted_practices: Use federated learning to enable multi-institutional AI training without sharing sensitive patient data.
Harmonize and standardize imaging protocols, common data elements, and interoperable data formats across sites for AI model development.
Establish global cooperation on a consistent regulatory framework for cross-border health data sharing.
Train AI models on diverse datasets to avoid bias and discrimination.
Ensure AI recommendations are reviewed by health care professionals before use.
Use differential privacy techniques to protect patient-level identifiers in secondary data analysis.
Conduct silent trial testing comparing AI recommendations with actual clinical decisions before deployment.
Engage patients and stakeholders in co-creation of AI tools.
Conduct information campaigns to raise public awareness of the use of anonymized medical data when explicit consent is impossible.
